text: What-if preview: before cancelling an idea or changing a share, show how value and priorities would shift across the graph
description: Major hypothesis loop 2026-11-22. RESEARCHED: Tankelevitch & Rintel, 'Goals as First-Class Abstractions in Human-AI Collaboration', AutomationXP26 workshop, CHI 2026 (Microsoft Research; PDF matthiasbaldauf.com/automationxp26/papers/AutomationXP26_paper_0982.pdf) name six capabilities a goal-oriented system should support: (1) goal articulation, (2) goals as first-class representations, (3) alignment and misalignment surfacing, (4) goal provenance and history, (5) outcome simulation: 'anticipate how decisions cascade across goal dependencies: lightweight what-if projections that move goal management from retrospective tracking to prospective reasoning', (6) situated goal support in workflows, incl. agents receiving delegated goals and reporting against them.\nOBSERVED mapping: (2) ideas are persistent git objects linked across servers; (3) value flow, path to root, duplicates, offers; (4) git history per idea (IdeaHistoryModal); (6) hooks and MCP put the idea into the agent's work, agents report in status comments; (1) partly (create_idea review, decomposition with hypotheses). (5) is missing: the value model already computes flows (calculateIdeaValues), but nothing shows the effect of a change before it is made.\nProposal: in the idea panel, hovering 'cancel' or dragging a share shows the shift: which ideas gain or lose value and priority, and the new top of the ranking. Pure client-side recalculation on a modified copy, nothing written. Smallest step: the same as a read-only MCP tool (what_if: cancel idea X / set share) so agents can reason prospectively first.

status.comment:
2026-11-22: built in two steps.
1. Read-only MCP tool what_if (mcp/tools/navigation.ts) over pure shared/what-if.ts: remove (ideas leave with their connections, as if deleted) or weight (a connection's raw weight); returns the ideas whose value or priority moves, largest move first, and the top 5 open ideas before/after. Found on the way: the value model ignores 'cancelled' (only implemented counts as done), so cancelling moves no numbers; removal is the meaningful what-if. On this repo's 951 ideas: 61 ms; removing 96e9fc41 shifts 45 ideas.
2. UI: the delete/remove dialog (IdeaRemovalDialog.vue, shown when a delete would take sub-ideas or an idea leaves its last list) now says 'Its value goes to: A, B, C', the three ideas that gain most, computed on the open space's own ideas.
Evidence: shared what-if.test, mcp tools-what-if.test (removal moves B's share to A, reweighting shifts B, nothing written), IdeaRemovalDialog.spec (names the gainer), frontend 472/472, mcp 72/72, shared 131/131, vue-tsc/tsc clean. MCP clients see what_if after /mcp reconnect.

Question for Felix: is the 'value goes to' line in the delete dialog useful as it reads, and should the same preview also show while dragging a connection's share?
